dse_runs.notes: Spec: 16-axis motor control, 32 simultaneous requests per 1us tick, all 32 results back within 0.44us p99. Batch throughput is the binding constraint: pipelined families with enough parallelism (m) are likely needed; unrolled_k with k>=32 may be too area-heavy. Keep accuracy >= 12 bits (max_abs_err <= 2^-12). Minimize luts+ffs.

final_text: Campaign complete. For the single spec **multiaxis_control** (16-axis motor control, 32 simultaneous requests per 1 µs tick, p99 batch ≤ 0.44 µs, error ≤ 2⁻¹², minimize LUTs+FFs), I spent the full 400-evaluation L1 budget on the structured DSE graph, which produced a 17-design feasible Pareto front dominated by pipelined_m families (m=2–4). L2 SimPy simulation of the top 5 confirmed all pass the system constraint, with the winner unchanged: **`pipelined_m: data_width=16, n_iter=15, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=1, rounding=round, m=3`** — 1225 LUTs+FFs (895 LUTs, 330 FFs), 12.4-bit accuracy (max error 2⁻¹²·⁴⁴), 124 Msps throughput, and simulated p99 batch latency of 0.305 µs (vs the 0.44 µs limit). The ladder sub-agent ran L3/L4/L5: no recorded verification, synthesis, or measured data existed for this exact configuration, so no estimates-vs-measured comparison was possible and no winner change was flagged (no reexplore needed). The spec was finalized on the L2 winner.
